manual_runtime_test_caveat: The recorded starter and reference outcomes cover this Pack's own behavioral contracts. The upstream project's full test suite was not run and is not claimed by this receipt.

notes: Only 11 of the 23 candidates change observable behaviour between 8.2.3 and 9.1.4. The 16 contracts are drawn from those 11 by splitting the multi-behaviour PRs (PR#437 covers four independent async extension points; PR#451 covers dispatch and the async strategy objects; PR#489 covers the pre-sleep and post-attempt log helpers separately). No demand was invented to reach the target count.

Four public demands are genuine public-API extensions rather than defect reports (stop_before_delay, wait_exception, the tenacity.asyncio.retry strategies, and the per-call statistics attribute). Per AUTHORING.md section 1 these are allowed to assert the presence of a public symbol only because the demand text spells out the required public name and signature, so the organization can derive it from the requirement instead of guessing upstream's naming.

Every other contract is written purely against names that already exist in the 8.2.3 starter tree, plus standard-library introspection attributes. No contract imports a helper introduced by the upstream fix.

The held-out four sit in the same capability families as the public twelve: three of them are further async extension points (wait/stop strategies, give-up callback, awaitable pause function for a synchronous callable) and one is the sibling log helper of the public logging demand.

Contract for PR#489's post-attempt helper drives the callback with a caller-controlled elapsed time instead of a measured one, because time.monotonic() on the Windows evaluator has a 15.6 ms resolution and a real short attempt measures exactly 0.0 s there.

rejected_candidates.reason: Annotation-only: rewrites a sys.version_info comparison so pyright can narrow it. Runtime behaviour is identical on both endpoints.
Formatter migration from black to ruff. Every hunk is reflow; no observable behaviour.

Internal refactor of the iteration loop into an action list. Net observable behaviour versus the starter is unchanged; the sequencing it enabled (computing the pause before evaluating the stop condition) is only observable through the stop_before_delay demand, which is authored against PR#423.
Ruff version bump; collapses overload bodies onto one line. No observable behaviour.

Fixes a recursion regression that PR#434 introduced inside this same window. Relative to the 8.2.3 starter the recursive-call behaviour is already correct, so no contract can separate the endpoints on it. The one net-new surface it leaves behind (per-call statistics on the wrapped function) is covered by the PR#484 demand.
Annotation-only: changes the declared return type of copy() to Self. The returned object was already self.__class__ on both endpoints.

Annotation-only: widens the match argument type to include re.Pattern. The starter already calls re.compile() on it, and re.compile() returns a compiled pattern unchanged, so a re.Pattern match argument works identically on both endpoints.
Python 3.14 support: CI matrix, classifiers, and a try/except-to-hasattr rewrite of two lazy properties. The rewrite is behaviour-preserving.
Annotation-only: introduces a logger Protocol so structlog/loguru type-check. Duck typing already accepted those objects at runtime on the starter.
Changes a mypy ignore code in a Tornado shim. No runtime effect, and Tornado is not installed in the evaluator runtime.

Drops Python 3.9 from metadata and CI and inlines the code that was gated behind version checks. On the 3.12 evaluator both endpoints take the same branch. Deletion-style change with no new behaviour.
Annotation-only: reshapes the decorator's overloads for an async sleep argument into a Protocol so pyright infers the return type correctly. Runtime dispatch is unchanged from PR#551.
